<description>
btck_chainstate_manager_process_block processes blocks as if they were requested. A block is therefore stored even if it has less work than the tip, is more than 288 blocks ahead of it, is below the minimum chain work, or was pruned before. bitcoind skips such blocks when it did not request them. This PR documents that a caller taking blocks from untrusted sources must apply these checks itself.

The header path is left undocumented on purpose, as discussed in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/33822#discussion_r2592425740; #34022, which proposed removing the flag, was closed. Blocks differ because force_processing changes what is stored. Tested: the kernel library builds and the whitespace and commit-message lints pass.
</description>

<commits>
ed2c4a344a kernel: document that process_block stores unrequested blocks

btck_chainstate_manager_process_block processes every block as
requested. Validation therefore does not skip a block that has less
work than the tip, is more than 288 blocks ahead of it, is below the
minimum chain work, or was pruned before. bitcoind skips such blocks
when it did not ask for them.

The API does not say so. Document that a caller taking blocks from
untrusted sources has to apply these checks itself.
</commits>
